name: Jun Zhu
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: I judge general language foundation-model pre-training to be mature, with thinned returns; but for narrow-domain video/world-model foundations, academia can still make adopted contributions, such as our own U-ViT.
D01.late_modes: General language foundation-model pre-training: already absorbed by a few vendors; academia can only analyze, not lead training.
D01.conflict: Shengshu trains video foundation models, so there is an interest in the judgment on narrow-domain foundation models.

D02.one_line: I have not discussed LLM RLVR, reward models or test-time compute publicly; this is outside my methods' coverage, so I make no judgment.

D03.one_line: My public material does not touch long-horizon credit assignment or self-improvement for digital agents at all, so I make no judgment.

D04.one_line: Agent harnesses and the tool-use ecosystem are outside my methods' coverage, so I make no judgment.

D05.one_line: Nobody looks after the trustworthiness of generated outputs, which makes it the scarcest research angle; Arena shows that academic methodological innovation can become a billion-dollar company.
D05.late_modes: Evaluation outsourcing with no new statistical methodology that simply hires more annotators to scale up is already commoditized.
D05.conflict: Vidu proves itself through third-party blind-test leaderboards, so there is an indirect interest in the judgment.

D06.one_line: The scarcity of real physical-interaction data (contact, force, friction) is the real bottleneck, not too little video pre-training; this is the 'data wall' I keep talking about.
D06.late_modes: Traditional VLAs that only imitate demonstration trajectories and cannot roll out futures have already been surpassed by generative methods.
D06.conflict: Motus/Motubrain bet on this direction, so there is a direct interest in the judgment.

D07.one_line: The training objectives for diffusion policy heads have not converged and academia still has room; but OpenVLA-OFT shows continuous actions have already overtaken them, and I do not dodge that.
D07.late_modes: Copying an off-the-shelf policy baseline without proposing a new objective is already saturated.
D07.conflict: His representative works are all on diffusion/flow, so there is a school-of-thought stake.

D08.one_line: Large video models were the first to achieve understanding and imagination and are new infrastructure connecting the digital and physical worlds; but L4 and L5 are the list of problems we set out, not solved.
D08.late_modes: A pure quality race of 'making video prettier and longer' has had its cost structure locked in and is meaningless.
D08.conflict: Shengshu's valuation and IPO narrative rest entirely on this judgment.

D09.one_line: Synthetic data/generative simulation is one realistic way to ease the 'data wall' (our own video-data pyramid follows this idea), but it cannot replace real interaction data.
D09.late_modes: Traditional simulation-engine work driven purely by rendering quality and containing no learning signal is being replaced by generative simulation.
D09.conflict: Motus's data-pyramid narrative depends on this assumption.

D10.one_line: I have not discussed autonomous driving publicly; inferring from the framework that 'track choice decides commercial scale', this is a track locked up by fleet data and capital, with limited room for academia.
D10.late_modes: Paper-style innovation in end-to-end planning has already been absorbed as an engineering problem by companies with fleet data.

D11.one_line: Efficiency gains in vision-language alignment are driven mainly by foundation-model vendors and will be internalized as a standard capability within 2-3 years; my own focus has always leaned more toward the generation side.
D11.late_modes: The stitched architecture of 'vision encoder, then connector, then LLM' is already standard and is no longer a selling point that can carry a good paper on its own.

D12.one_line: Diffusion/flow foundations, few-step generation and unified understanding and generation still have mechanism-level problems with no consensus; this is one of the directions where my methods overlap the most.
D12.late_modes: A video-generation race that purely chases quality and duration has had its cost structure locked in by a few big companies.
D12.conflict: Vidu's core business; Bayesian-school background and a preference for the diffusion route.

D13.one_line: I have not discussed mechanistic interpretability or alignment research publicly, so I make no judgment.

D14.one_line: Fast samplers such as DPM-Solver show that academia can make systems-efficiency contributions that frameworks absorb, but this is not my main battlefield, so I do not judge in depth.

D15.one_line: No public material touches AI for Science; weakly inferred from my general belief that 'theory must be tested in real settings', and a conservative score given.

D16.one_line: The generative rebuilding of recommender systems is far from my research framework and I have taken no public position, so a conservative score is given.

lever_reason: Real physical-interaction data (the data wall) and world models that can close the loop by predicting actions are the real bottlenecks of physical AI; the scarcity of evaluation and calibration is badly underestimated; the marginal return of purely scaled foundation models has thinned.

Q2.condition: Narrow-domain model (VLA, video or world model, not general LLM pre-training) + credible third-party evaluation in that domain + open weights that can be adopted externally; no need to pile on large compute.

cruxes.question: Are video generation models really building a true 'world model', or just interpolating within the distribution?
cruxes.my_position: Video was the first to achieve 'understanding and imagination' and is a necessary link in the closed loop; but L4 and L5 are the list of problems we set out, and they are not yet solved.
cruxes.would_change_if: An independent team reproduces video-model prediction errors significantly below the baseline in out-of-distribution physical scenarios (contacts and collisions unlike the training distribution).

cruxes.question: Which should be the default for robot policies: a diffusion/flow action head, or an autoregressive/continuous action representation?
cruxes.my_position: The diffusion head has a theoretical advantage on multimodal action distributions, but OpenVLA-OFT shows continuous actions have already overtaken it on some real-robot tasks, and that cannot be dodged.
cruxes.would_change_if: On the same real-robot benchmark, seeing the diffusion head clearly overtake continuous action representations on contact-rich, strongly multimodal tasks, rather than merely tying on well-structured tasks.

cruxes.question: Is LLM/agent evaluation really 'grunt work with no impact', or an underrated methodological opportunity?
cruxes.my_position: Hiring more annotators or tuning more judge prompts is indeed grunt work; but Arena shows that crowdsourcing + Elo as a methodological innovation can create huge value, and the key is the new mechanism.
cruxes.would_change_if: Seeing a new evaluation methodology (not more annotation) shown to reveal systematic biases that existing judges cannot detect, and adopted by the industry.

taste_advice: First ask whether the result means the model has learned real physical/causal structure or is just interpolating within the given distribution; do not train generation, prediction and action separately and evaluate them separately.

pairwise.why: The ten-year impact ceiling of world models is higher than that of evaluation infrastructure, even though evaluation itself is underrated.
A closed loop that can drive real actions is more decisive than pure evaluation infrastructure.
If it stops at world generation (L1), the story runs out; a closed loop that can drive action is the destination.
D07 already models prediction and action jointly, which is more complete than a pure world representation.
Simulation/synthetic data is a tool for filling the data-wall gap; robot learning itself is the destination.
Both are outside my methods; continual learning is at least still a question of model capability, not a pure engineering problem.
Generation is where my comparative advantage lies, and it also connects more directly to 'imagination', an element of a world model.
Evaluation and calibration are scarcer than piling on more parameters; in my view the marginal return of general pre-training has thinned.
D04 is closer to scaffolding engineering; learning and self-improvement at least still point at model capability itself.
I have not discussed alignment research publicly; evaluation and calibration are closer to my real work experience.
Autonomous driving is locked up by fleet data and capital; the academic space in robot learning is more familiar to me.
